idea: Replace random order with a target-domain filter plus dedup and damage removal. (1) Exact-dedup docs by hash of normalised text (keep first). (2) Drop junk: docs whose line-level repetition is high (unique lines / total lines < 0.5 for docs with >=4 lines) or whose zlib compression ratio (compressed/raw bytes) is < 0.2. (3) Score domain: fit a char n-gram (1-3, analyzer='char_wb' or word 1-2gram) HashingVectorizer + TF-IDF logistic regression with positives = target_sample (chunked into ~1500-char pieces) and negatives = a seeded random sample of ~3000 pool-doc chunks; also add cheap WikiText-style features: starts with '= ' title line, frequency of ' @-@ ', ' @,@ ', ' @.@ ', ' , ', ' . ' tokens. Keep docs with classifier probability above a threshold chosen so pool docs resembling the target (WikiText-style articles) are retained. (4) Remove word-shuffled damaged WikiText docs: build a word-bigram set from target_sample plus the high-confidence pool docs and compute for each candidate the fraction of its word bigrams that appear in that set (or simpler: rate of common function bigrams such as 'of the', 'in the', ', and', '. The', 'to the' per 1000 words, and the rate of impossible bigrams such as ', ,', '. ,', 'the the', 'of of', ', .'); drop docs whose well-formed-bigram rate is below ~half the median of the target_sample rate. (5) Count tokens of survivors with tiktoken gpt2; return survivors in seeded shuffled order; if they total less than T just return them (trainer cycles), and if more than T keep the highest-scoring ones up to ~T before shuffling.
why: The pool is about half off-domain web text, boilerplate, duplicates and word-shuffled WikiText, so spending all T tokens on clean, in-domain, well-ordered WikiText-style articles should cut held-out bpb far more than any ordering trick.

idea:
Rewrite the filter as a robust pipeline with fallbacks, so it can never return an empty list. Experiment 2 most likely died because its hard gates removed every document.

1. Normalise: for each doc, s = doc.strip(); key = ' '.join(s.split()).lower(). Exact-dedup on key, keeping the first occurrence. Do not use prefix dedup.

2. Loose format gate (wiki-like): keep a doc if len(s) >= 200 and either s.startswith('=') or the doc contains at least one of ' @-@ ', ' @,@ ', ' @.@ ', or its rate of ' , ' plus ' . ' is at least 3 per 100 whitespace tokens. Do not use a strict title regex.

3. Damage filter for word-shuffled articles: build S, the set of lowercased whitespace-token bigrams from target docs 0-99. For any text, h = fraction of its first 3000 token bigrams that are in S. Compute h on target docs 100-199 and take the median m. Keep wiki-like pool docs with h >= 0.6 * m. Print the counts and the h quantiles for debugging.

4. Junk guards: drop docs whose zlib compressed/raw ratio is < 0.2, or whose lowercased text contains 'click here to order', 'free shipping' or 'best price guaranteed'.

5. Fallbacks: if survivors have fewer than 200 docs, relax step 3 to h >= 0.4 * m. If still fewer than 200, use all wiki-like deduped docs. If still empty, use all deduped docs.

6. Output: shuffle survivors with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED', 0))) and return [int(i) for i in survivors], as plain Python ints that index the original docs list. Do not pad with off-domain docs; the trainer cycles a short list.
why: Training only on clean, deduplicated WikiText-style articles (dropping spam, web text and word-shuffled copies) should cut bpb well below the raw pool, and the loose gates plus fallbacks avoid the empty-result crash of experiment 2.
outcome: dev 1.8343 against 1.9618 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

idea:
Keep the current pipeline (exact dedup, loose wiki gate, junk guards, fallbacks, seeded shuffle, no padding) but replace the single loose damage threshold (h >= 0.6 * median on the first 3000 bigrams) with calibrated, window-level damage detection.

1. Build S_half (lowercased whitespace-token bigrams) and V_half (lowercased token vocabulary) from target docs 0-99.

2. For any text, split its full token sequence, not just the first 3000 tokens, into consecutive windows of 250 tokens; drop a final window shorter than 100 tokens unless it is the only one. Per window compute (a) the bigram hit rate against S_half and (b) the unigram hit rate against V_half. Per doc take h_mean = mean bigram hit rate over windows, h_min = minimum bigram hit rate over windows, u_min = minimum unigram hit rate over windows.

3. Calibrate on target docs 100-199: compute the same three statistics and take the 2nd percentile of each, p_mean, p_min, p_u.

4. Keep a wiki-like pool doc only if h_mean >= 0.9 * p_mean AND h_min >= 0.85 * p_min AND u_min >= 0.9 * p_u. This removes fully word-shuffled articles, partly or locally shuffled ones, and character-corrupted ones.

5. Tighten the format gate: the stripped doc must start with '= ' and its first line must end with '='. As a fallback, if this strict gate leaves fewer than 200 docs, use the current loose gate.

6. Keep the zlib and spam-phrase guards and the existing fallback chain: if fewer than 200 survivors, multiply the three thresholds by 0.7, then fall back to the wiki-like docs, then to all deduped docs.

7. Print the number of survivors, their total gpt2 token count as a fraction of T, and the quantiles of the three statistics for pool and target. Return plain ints in seeded shuffled order.

Implementation note: compute everything in one pass over the deduped docs; do not use list.index lookups.
why: The 0.6 * median threshold on only the first 3000 bigrams probably lets through partly or locally shuffled and character-damaged articles and loosely gated non-wiki text, so thresholds calibrated on held-out target docs at window level should give a cleaner in-domain training set.

1. Pass 1: run the current filter as it is (S from target docs 0-99, h on the first 3000 bigrams, keep h >= 0.6*m, then junk guards). Call the result A and keep h1 for each doc.

2. Bootstrap a larger reference set S2: the lowercased whitespace-token bigrams of target docs 0-99, plus all bigrams of the docs in A whose h1 is at or above the median h1 of A. These are the most clearly clean pool articles.

3. Rescore: h2 = fraction of a doc's first 3000 bigrams that are in S2. For a pool doc that contributed to S2, this is biased upward, which is acceptable because those docs are already the clean ones.

4. Calibrate the threshold on target docs 100-199, which are not in S2:
   - clean = h2 of each doc;
   - damaged = h2 of the same docs after shuffling tokens within consecutive blocks of 10 tokens, using the seeded rng.

5. Survivors B = docs in A with h2 >= thr. Docs that contributed to S2 are kept automatically.

6. Safety: if B has fewer than 60% of the gpt2 tokens of A (estimate tokens as len(doc)/4 to save time), or fewer than 200 docs, return A, which is the current best behaviour. Otherwise return B.

7. Print |A|, |B|, thr, and the quantiles of clean, damaged and pool h2. Return plain ints in seeded shuffled order. Use a dict or enumerate for index mapping, not list.index.
why: The 0.6*median threshold on a 100-document bigram set probably lets many word-shuffled articles through; a larger bootstrapped reference set with a threshold calibrated on synthetically shuffled target docs should separate them more cleanly, and the fallback to the current selection guards against the over-pruning that likely sank experiment 4.
